subject: vacancy is an input, not a universal rule
preheader: use property history and current leasing evidence.
headline: Vacancy isn't pessimism. It's accounting.
body: Tenant turnover, cleaning, repairs, marketing, lease-up time, concessions, and credit loss can reduce collected rent. The appropriate assumption depends on the property and operating plan.

Review the property's lease and collection history, current comparable listings and leases, time-on-market evidence, planned tenant profile, and any short-term-rental seasonality that actually applies.

For illustration, $1,800 monthly rent is $21,600 per year. An entered 5% vacancy assumption reduces modeled income by $1,080; an entered 10% assumption reduces it by $2,160. The $1,080 difference shows sensitivity, not which percentage is correct.
Use more than one scenario when evidence is uncertain, and record why the selected vacancy assumption fits the specific property.

TrueCap starts a new analysis with a generic 5% vacancy assumption. It is editable, not market-specific, so replace it with evidence from the property's operating history and local leasing conditions before relying on the result.
